title: SvelteKit load guards and focus
summary: Implement a load-time checkout decision, then review a page that renders for anonymous visitors and never announces the new view.

scenario.briefing: The checkout page renders before the session is known, and keyboard users stay on the old navigation after the route changes.

objectives.description: Decide access in a load function before rendering.
Review a page for load-time and accessibility risks.

hints: Return a redirect to /login for a signed-out visitor.
Return a redirect to /cart for an empty cart.
Return the item count only when checkout may render.

misconceptions.description: Rendering checkout and checking access later.
misconceptions.testDescription: Signed-out visitors are redirected to login.
misconceptions.feedback: A load guard prevents the page from rendering at all. Checking after render flashes private content and wastes work.

misconceptions.description: Loading checkout with an empty cart.
misconceptions.testDescription: An empty cart is redirected to the cart page.
misconceptions.feedback: Checkout with no items cannot complete. Redirect to the cart so the user can add something first.

misconceptions.description: Accepting a page that never focuses or announces the new view.
misconceptions.feedback: A missing load guard and a silent route change are functional defects. Block the change until both are fixed.

sections.title: Load runs before the page
sections.body: A SvelteKit load function can redirect before a component renders. Use it for access and cart checks so the checkout page never flashes for an ineligible visitor.

sections.title: Redirect with a reason
sections.body: Anonymous visitors belong at sign-in; a signed-in visitor with an empty cart belongs at the catalog. Distinct redirects let the next page explain what is missing.

sections.title: A page change needs an announcement
sections.body: Client-side navigation does not reload the document. Move focus to the heading and update the title so keyboard and screen reader users know the view changed.

steps.title: Review the checkout page
steps.prompt: Review +page.svelte and select every real access or accessibility problem.
hints: Check whether access is decided before the page renders.
Look for focus or title updates after navigation.
Check whether the back action is a real link.
Reject findings that describe a load function or title the file does not contain.

artifact.title: +page.svelte
artifact.caption: The page renders checkout for an anonymous visitor and never focuses the heading or announces the view.
artifact.content:
Checkout

{#if !signedIn}

Please sign in.

{/if}

findings.label: The page renders for an anonymous visitor instead of redirecting in load.
The page never focuses the heading or announces the new checkout view.
The back action uses a button with goto instead of a link, so it cannot be opened in a new tab.
A load function already redirects an empty cart.
The page sets a descriptive document title for checkout.

verdicts.label: Block the change until the listed risks are fixed.
Ship it; the remaining concerns are cosmetic.
Only formatting and naming need work.

steps.explanation: The page has no load guard, so an anonymous visitor sees checkout. It also has no focus or title update, and the back action is a button rather than a link. There is no load function in the artifact.

accessibility.summary: The workspace is keyboard accessible. Use the editor with Tab and run checks with Ctrl+Enter; every result is announced in text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Tab moves between the editor, hints, and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks. Hint buttons reveal one level at a time.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, pass or fail state, and the missing or forbidden source fragment.
